protocol.py: 5 biology problems (4 warnings, 1 note).

1. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was loaded but never set
   line 57:  p20.aspirate(2, block["A1"])
   At line 57 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3 and A4 in slot 1, on a temperature
   module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until
   `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), ligase (reagent), vector and water
   (carrier) sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 96 times over the
   run. The person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells
   A1, A2, A3 and A4 in slot 1.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3 and A4 in slot 1.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24
   Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 1, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at
   the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html
   Source: Thermo Fisher T4 ligase manual: keep on ice, use within minutes
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/t4dnaligase_1U_man.pdf
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   [a6c179281f31]

2. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: ligase
   line 62:  p20.dispense(1, plate[dest_well])
   At line 62 the robot put ligase into wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in
   slot 2 (this line did it 11 times). Take well A1 in slot 2: at that moment it held only 2
   ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 76, to make the 11 ul
   of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is
   meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought
   the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many
   times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star
   activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 2:
   water and buffer first, then the sample, then ligase last. Or make a master mix of water,
   buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [d1fe8cc75fa3]

3. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: vector (well A3 in slot 1)
   line 65:  p20.aspirate(3, block["A3"])
   At line 65 the tip went into vector (well A3 in slot 1) while it still carried buffer
   (well A1 in slot 1) and ligase (well A2 in slot 1) from an earlier step. A tip that has
   touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now
   holds material that does not belong there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards,
   but only into wells that were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not
   harmed. What is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: well A3 in slot 1.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 65 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [58ad878242a6]

4. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 24 stocks
   line 69:  p20.aspirate(5, inserts_plate[src_insert_well])
   At line 69 the tip went into insert 1 (well A1 in slot 4), insert 2 (well A2 in slot 4),
   insert 3 (well A3 in slot 4), insert 4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 20 more while it still

findings.title: A temperature module was loaded but never set
findings.explanation: At line 57 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3 and A4 in slot 1, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), ligase (reagent), vector and water (carrier) sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 96 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3 and A4 in slot 1.
findings.fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24 Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 1, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: ligase
findings.explanation: At line 62 the robot put ligase into wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 2 (this line did it 11 times). Take well A1 in slot 2: at that moment it held only 2 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 76, to make the 11 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 2: water and buffer first, then the sample, then ligase last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: vector (well A3 in slot 1)
findings.explanation: At line 65 the tip went into vector (well A3 in slot 1) while it still carried buffer (well A1 in slot 1) and ligase (well A2 in slot 1) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 65 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.
